done_when: When close or land merges the default branch into an item's branch in Forge's own repo, it refreshes the synced guide copies in the same merge, so a merged guide change never fails the synced-copies test on another branch

known.title: Refresh mirrored guides when canonical skill sources change
Follow-up: Distinguish new guide repairs from existing branch edits

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - main changes a canonical guide such as `.codex/skills/test-audit/SKILL.md`, and close merges it into an open branch.
The incoming-change filter excludes canonical guide sources outside `src/forge/templates`. `review.py:58-62` renders both hosts' test-audit copies from that Codex file through `sync._synced_text` (`sync.py:427-430`). Consequently, this merge returns before refreshing the Claude copy, leaving the hosts with different guidance. The same omission affects `.codex/skills/app-baseline/SKILL.md` and `.codex/skills/forge/fde.md`, used by `app_baseline.py:142` and `story.py:103-104`. Include these existing renderer inputs in the refresh trigger.
findings.title: Refresh mirrored guides when canonical skill sources change

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 2
Case: normal use - an already checked branch changes guide templates and their synced copies, while main advances in an unrelated file.
This comparison includes all guide differences between main and the item branch, including edits already checked before the merge. It therefore sets `overlap` even when the merge required no guide repair. Lines 143-159 then publish another head and wait for CI instead of preserving the previously checked head. Compare the guide changes introduced by the merge and refresh, so existing guide edits alone do not trigger another CI round. The added close-only test does not exercise this merge retention decision.
findings.title: Follow-up: Distinguish new guide repairs from existing branch edits

why: When main changes Forge's guide templates, every open branch that merges main fails tests/test_tools_guide.py test_9 in CI because its synced guide copies (.claude and .codex skills) are now stale, costing a repair round and a full CI wait; this happened four times on 6 Nov 2026
